seo.title: United Airlines: NLX self-service voicebot - 64% of wheelchair requests automated (2025)
seo.meta_description: United Airlines automates 64% of wheelchair requests (90% CSAT) and 31% of flight cancellations with NLX by voice and chat, to absorb 30 million calls a year.
seo.resume_citable: United Airlines connected the NLX platform to its contact center and automated 64% of wheelchair requests (90% CSAT) and 31% of flight cancellations through voice and chat.

faq.q: What does United Airlines' AI self-service do?
faq.a: It lets a traveler cancel a flight, check a bag, or add an accessibility request through voice or chat, without waiting for an agent, and hands off to a human outside the automated scope.
64% of wheelchair requests automated with 90% CSAT, and 31% of flight cancellations automated with 82% CSAT, over a 6-month base.

objectif_business: Absorb a call volume that had become unmanageable after post-covid traffic recovery, by letting travelers handle frequent actions themselves (cancellation, baggage, adding a wheelchair or a service animal) without waiting for an agent.
description: United connected the NLX platform to its contact journey to automate specific requests through voice and chat. A traveler who calls or writes can cancel a flight, check a bag, or add an accessibility request to their reservation within minutes, guided by an assistant that understands the request in natural language and executes the action in United's systems. When a case falls outside the automated scope, the handoff goes to an agent. The rollout targets first the high-volume, low-variability requests, where automation holds without degrading the experience.
points_cles: Self-service voicebot for cancellations, baggage, and accessibility requests.
NLX platform in voice and chat, connected to the IVR and United's PNR.
64% of wheelchair requests automated (90% CSAT), 31% of cancellations.
Evidence B, confirmed status, results measured over six months.

resultats.metrique: CSAT on wheelchair and assistance requests
Annual call volume that prompted the project (2022)

niveau_preuve.justification: A quantified NLX platform case study (automation rates, CSAT and the starting call volume). Every figure comes from the vendor: no independent source repeats them. The TechCrunch article documents United's AI practice and its move to a conversational agent on United.com, but mentions neither NLX nor the wheelchair and cancellation automations; it sets the context, it does not corroborate the figures.

stack_technique.detail: Multimodal conversational AI platform (voice and chat) that understands the request in natural language and executes the action in United's systems.
Contact center phone channel to which the assistant is connected.
Live access to the reservation record, a condition for executing cancellations, baggage, and accessibility requests.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Real time, on each incoming call or conversation.
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: United's contact center Service Transformation team, with the NLX platform.
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: The intent expressed by the traveler, matched against the reservation record live. Without reliable access to the PNR and the inventory systems, the assistant cannot execute the action and shifts everything to the agent, which cancels the gain.

etapes.detail: The traveler calls or writes and states their request in natural language (cancel, check a bag, add a wheelchair).
The assistant identifies the intent and checks whether the case falls into an automated scenario.
For a case within scope, the action is carried out in United's systems and confirmed to the traveler.
Outside scope or on failure, the record and the context are transferred to a human advisor.

prerequis_data: API access to the reservation system (PNR)
a map of the high-volume intents
prerequis_orga: a contact center team ready to co-design the scenarios
governance of the escalation to the agent
a compliance framework for voice and sensitive data
replication.premiere_etape: Choose a high-volume, low-variability intent (e.g. cancellation) and automate it end to end before widening.

playbook.action: Map the high-volume, low-variability intents (cancellation, baggage, accessibility) and prioritize them by volume and risk.
playbook.livrable: A prioritized list of intents with annual volumes.

playbook.action: Connect the conversational platform to the PNR and the IVR, write the business rules for the first request.
playbook.livrable: A first end-to-end automated scenario in pre-production.

playbook.action: Pilot on one intent with systematic escalation to the agent; measure automation rate and CSAT per scenario.
playbook.livrable: A pilot review (automation, CSAT, failures and causes).

playbook.action: Extend to the following intents and lock down compliance (voice, sensitive data such as accessibility requests).
playbook.livrable: A catalog of scenarios in production and a permanent dashboard.

replication.equipe: 1 contact center PM + 1 integration dev (PNR/IVR) + 1 compliance lead; the vendor supports scenario design.

statut_vivant.note: NLX self-service documented as active, with results measured over six months and external recognition (Opus Research Conversational AI Award 2024) for the automated addition of a wheelchair and a service animal.

transposable_ue.note: A voice and chat self-service to handle cancellations, baggage, and accessibility requests is transposable to the EU. Recording and processing the voice requires a GDPR legal basis and explicit consent; the AI Act requires informing the customer they are talking to an AI. Implicit health data (wheelchair, service animal) falls under sensitive categories to frame.
